statement: MUSIC-SUITE P7, owner decision #37 (signed 2026-09-26): six public-domain US sound recordings on the Flip's shelf. Each is a US sound recording published before 1925 (public domain under the Music Modernization Act, 2018) of a composition also out of copyright, downloaded from the exact page and file decision #37 names, with the three checks (transfer from the original disc, the archive's terms, the matrix/take) confirmed and recorded under `checks`. Trimmed for leading/trailing silence only (scripts/music/pd-shelf/trim_convert.py) and converted to MP3; nothing else in the audio was changed. The composition-side public-domain reasoning for each recording lives in lib/babylon/music/pdShelf.ts (PD_SHELF[].whyFree), not repeated here.

files.title: Livery Stable Blues

checks.transfer: LOC National Jukebox item page: 'Recording Repository: Source of original recording: Recorded Sound Section, Library of Congress' -- a transfer of the physical Victor 18255 disc, not a reissue.
checks.terms: The item page's own National Jukebox notice: recordings published before 1923 are public domain under the Music Modernization Act and free to copy, modify, distribute and perform, even commercially, without permission.
checks.matrixTake: Item page: 'Victor 18255. Matrix/Take: B-19331/1.' -- matches Victor 18255-B (the file_id is dlc_victor_18255_01_b19331_01).

files.accessNote: www.loc.gov/item/jukebox-186254/ itself served a Cloudflare 'verify you are human' challenge, which was not attempted or solved. The item's own facts (repository, rights notice, matrix/take) were read from a Wayback Machine capture of that page (web.archive.org/web/20250203061733), and the audio was fetched directly from the media file that page embeds, tile.loc.gov (a plain 200 response, audio/mpeg, no challenge).

checks.transfer: archive.org item metadata: collection ['78rpm','audio_music'], source '78' -- a transfer of the physical 78rpm disc, uploaded 2004 (predating archive.org's Great 78 Project and the post-2023 major-label agreement that restricts some of that project's later uploads).
checks.terms: No licenseurl or restrictive rights statement on the item; a US sound recording published in 1920 is public domain since 2022-01-01 under the Music Modernization Act regardless.
checks.matrixTake: Item notes: 'Okeh-4169 (7529 take C)', matching OKeh 4169 take C in the candidate table; corroborated by the Wikimedia Commons file (commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mamie_Smith,_Crazy_Blues.ogg), which credits this same archive.org item and repeats 'Okeh-4169 (7529 take C)' in its own description.

checks.transfer: Commons file description: 'Credit: 78 RPM disc' -- a transfer of the physical disc.
checks.terms: Commons file's own License/Permission fields: UsageTerms 'Public domain', Copyrighted 'False', with the uploader's stated reasoning that both the 1923 Columbia sound recording and the 1922 Hunter/Austin composition have expired; carries the PD-old-auto-record-expired and CC-PD-Mark categories.
checks.matrixTake: Recording date on the file page, 1923-02-16, matches the candidate table's 'recorded Feb 1923'. The file page does not itself print the Columbia A3844 catalog number, so this one check rests on date, artist and title, not a matrix number -- noted as the least certain of the three.
